data.gist: Authors argue BMAX's bone-core harvesting captures bone-adherent MSCs missed by aspiration, which may contribute to the greater adherence, proliferation, and clonogenicity observed.
data.plain: The discussion frames why the new preparation might work better: standard aspiration pulls out fluid and is biased toward fat-lineage stromal cells, whereas cells tightly attached to bone surfaces — reportedly the most clonogenic ones — are largely missed. Because BMAX harvests bone cores with their extracellular matrix intact, the authors suggest, in hedged terms, that capturing this bone-associated population may explain the better cell behavior they saw.
